blocks.text: While dialysis can be life-saving for people with kidney failure, there are several problems associated with this treatment.

items: Dialysis requires access to the bloodstream, which increases the risk of infections.
Hypotension, or low blood pressure, is a common complication of haemodialysis.
Muscle cramps can occur during dialysis due to changes in salt levels.
Dialysis can cause anaemia, which can lead to fatigue and weakness.
If too much fluid is removed too quickly, it can lead to dehydration or low blood pressure.
Dialysis treatments can be emotionally challenging. Patients may feel anxious, depressed, or overwhelmed by the demands of the treatment.
